subject: POC session orchestration — prompts, routing, and load windows
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Nora Patel <nora.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Kai Reynolds <kai.reynolds@dataforge.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC kickoff + working session — scheduling

Hi Nora,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. We'd like to lock in a 2-hour hands-on POC kickoff where we run through: an inventory of your prompts, routing/guardrail requirements, and a short load window to validate throughput and cache behavior. Goals: surface any structured-output constraints, confirm routing fallbacks, and run two 10–15 minute load bursts later in the week.

Would any of these windows work for your team (PT):
- Tue Nov 24, 10:00–12:00
- Wed Nov 25, 13:00–15:00
- Fri Nov 27, 09:00–11:00 (shorter window if needed)

If none of those fit, send a couple alternatives. I’ll loop in our SEs to bring a prompt inventory template and the runbook.

Agenda (draft):
- 15m introductions & success criteria
- 40m prompt inventory & structured output requirements
- 25m routing/guardrails + fallbacks discussion
- 20m load test prep & scheduling
- 20m live mini-load bursts + next steps

Attachments: POC-runbook-v2.xlsx (draft plan) — I’ll add a lightweight prompt inventory template right after this.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
(415) 555-0137

Hi Ben,

Thanks — we’re excited to get this going. A couple conflicts next week: Nov 24 is a holiday here and Nov 25 we have leadership offsite in the afternoon. Can we aim for the week after? Proposed slots (EST):
- Tue Dec 1, 10:30–12:30
- Wed Dec 2, 14:00–16:00

Also: a quick ask from our security/compliance manager — please confirm the load windows will not include production tokens and that logs/audit for the session are retained only per our onboarding agreement. I’ll bring our lead product manager and the infra engineer who will run the in-house checks.

Thanks,

Forwarding Nora's availability and the compliance note. Marissa, Lauren — looping you both to coordinate the hands-on portion. Key asks from Acme:
- Confirm non-production tokens and audit retention (security)
- Prompt inventory + structured output constraints (PM)
- A short load plan we can run during the session (two 10–15 minute bursts) and a preferred window (they suggested Dec 1/2)

Attachments included here: prompt-inventory-acme.csv (template), POC-runbook-v2.xlsx, network-checklist.pdf (they may share environment IP allowlist).

My suggested slot: Tue Dec 1, 10:30–12:30 EST (that’s 07:30–09:30 PT). If that works, can we finalize agenda and ownership? Recommended ownership:
- Marissa: prompt walkthrough, structured-output examples, guardrails
- Lauren: load test orchestration + post-test observations
- Ben: overall cadence, mutual action items, follow-ups and billing/procurement checkpoints

Also: Marissa, can you add a short pre-read (1-pager) for Acme that covers what to prepare in their prompt inventory so we can be hands-on right away? I attached the CSV template — feel free to tailor it.

Ben

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Ben/Nora — Tue Dec 1, 10:30–12:30 EST works for our team. Confirming a few operational items so the session is productive:

1) Security/compliance: we will use a sandboxed account with non-production API keys for the load bursts. We'll export session-level logs and place them in a customer-specific folder with the retention agreed in the onboarding doc (see runbook link).

2) Prompt inventory & pre-read: attached a one-page pre-read (sent as an inline note below) and the tailored prompt-inventory-acme.csv. Please ask the PM to pre-fill 20–30 representative prompts with expected structured outputs (field names, types, failure modes). The pre-read outlines a short mapping for structured-output validation.

3) Load windows & routing test plan: propose two 10-minute bursts during minute 45–55 and minute 100–110 of the session to validate batching and KV cache behavior. We’ll instrument per-request timing and token counts and share a post-test summary. If Acme wants a quieter window, we can reduce to one burst.

4) Agenda tweak: move structured-output examples earlier (after intros) so we can craft guardrails before the routing discussion. Updated agenda below:
- 10:30–10:45 Intro & success criteria
- 10:45–11:15 Structured-output examples + guardrails (Marissa)
- 11:15–11:40 Prompt inventory walkthrough (Nora + Marissa)
- 11:40–12:00 Routing & fallback policies (Marissa)
- 12:00–12:15 Load bursts (Lauren)
- 12:15–12:30 Wrap, action items, next steps (Ben)

Attachments referenced: prompt-inventory-acme.csv (attached), short-pre-read-POC.pdf (inline summary), POC-runbook-v2.xlsx (shared drive).

Lauren — quick confirm if you’re good to run the load bursts at those minutes; a one-line is fine.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
